requirements.text: The user must undo and redo its last thousand actions.
The product must count and display the time that the user uses to play.
The product must count and display the number of the user'saction.
The product must record the score (time and number of counts) of a play associated with the name of a user.
The product must display a window with all the player'sscores.
The main window shall provide the following parts : A board, see chapter 3.2.1.1. a menu bar, see chapter 3.2.5.
The user can cancel a movement.
The user can redo a movement that has been canceled.
The following statistics are recorded during the game : number of block movements since the start. time since the start.
The user could erase all the statistics.
Open a previous saved game.
Save the current game.
Stop the game
The application must validate the integrity and structure of any saved game file before loading it to prevent malicious data injection.
The application must ensure that the statistics file is stored in a location with restricted write access, and the application must handle file I/O errors securely without leaking system paths.
Define a structured, versioned file format (e.g., JSON or XML) for saved games to ensure data integrity and backward compatibility.
Implement a circular buffer or limit the undo/redo history to a reasonable number (e.g., 1000) to prevent excessive memory consumption and file bloat.
The application must restore the board state within 100ms of an undo/redo request, and the memory footprint for the 1000-action history buffer must not exceed 50MB.
Save operations must complete within 500ms, and the resulting save file size must not exceed 1MB.

OPEN: There is no specification for handling file I/O errors during the 'Save' or 'Open' processes beyond a generic error message. - Specify error handling strategies for common failure modes such as disk full, permission denied, or file corruption during save/load operations.

OPEN: The statistics management system is limited to 10 entries, but there is no requirement for how the system handles concurrent access or file locking if multiple instances or processes attempt to access the statistics file. - The application must implement file-level locking to ensure data integrity during concurrent read/write operations on the statistics file.
